title: Problem 01
markdown:
Prove that $3^n 2^{3n} - 1$ is divisible by 23 for every positive integer $n$.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
### Method 1: Modular Arithmetic

$$
3^n 2^{3n} - 1 = 24^n - 1
$$

$$
24 \equiv 1 \pmod{23}
$$

$$
24^n - 1 \equiv 1^n - 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{23}
$$

$$
\therefore\ 23 \mid (3^n 2^{3n} - 1).
$$

### Method 2: Factorization

**Identity:**

$$
x^n - 1 = (x - 1)(x^{n-1} + \dots + 1)
$$

**Solution:**

$$
3^n 2^{3n} - 1 = 24^n - 1
$$

$$
= (24 - 1)(24^{n-1} + \dots + 1)
$$

$$
= 23(24^{n-1} + \dots + 1)
$$

$$
\therefore\ 23 \mid (3^n 2^{3n} - 1).
$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Combining exponents gives $3^n 2^{3n} - 1 = 24^n - 1$. Method 1 uses [modular arithmetic](#node/node-modular-arithmetic/sec-modular-arithmetic-core) with $24 \equiv 1 \pmod{23} \implies 24^n - 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{23}$. Method 2 uses [algebraic factorization](#node/node-algebraic-factorization/sec-algebraic-factorization-core) via $x^n - 1 = (x - 1)(x^{n-1} + \dots + 1)$ with $x = 24$ to factor out 23.

### Key Technique
[Modular arithmetic](#node/node-modular-arithmetic/sec-modular-arithmetic-core) ($24 \equiv 1 \pmod{23}$) and [algebraic factorization](#node/node-algebraic-factorization/sec-algebraic-factorization-core) of $x^n - 1$.
